from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "Think of a vector as a movement in space.",
            "We start at the origin (0,0).",
            "Moving along x and y creates a path.",
            "Meet i-hat and j-hat, our basic unit steps.",
            "Every vector is a combination of these steps."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        IHAT_COLOR = "#58C4DD"

        i_hat = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,0), buff=0, color=IHAT_COLOR, stroke_width=4)

        main_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(3,2), buff=0, color=VEC_COLOR, stroke_width=6)

        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.play(FadeIn(pixel), Write(pixel_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        path_x = Line(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(3,0), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        path_y = Line(plane.c2p(3,0), plane.c2p(3,2), color=WHITE, stroke_width=2, stroke_opacity=0.4)
        
        self.play(
            pixel.animate.move_to(plane.c2p(3,0)),
            Create(path_x),
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.play(
            pixel.animate.move_to(plane.c2p(3,2)),
            Create(path_y),
            pixel_label.animate.next_to(plane.c2p(3,2), UR),
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(IHAT_COLOR)
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(i_hat), Write(i_label),
            GrowArrow(j_hat), Write(j_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(VEC_COLOR)
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(main_vec),
            Write(vec_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(path_x), FadeOut(path_y), run_time=1)
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Concept of Linear Transformation"
        lines = [
            "Transformations warp space while keeping the origin fixed.",
            "Grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced.",
            "Imagine stretching a rubber sheet without tearing."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Pre-define colors for readability
        LINE_HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW
        GRID_COLOR = "#444444"
        ORIGIN_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        FLASH_COLOR = "#AAFFCC"

        # Initialize the coordinate grid (NumberPlane)
        # We constrain it to a 4x4 coordinate range to fit well within the right-side area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            y_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": GRID_COLOR,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.6
            },
            axis_config={"stroke_color": GRID_COLOR}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Create the origin dot
        origin_dot = Dot(plane.c2p(0, 0), color=ORIGIN_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        origin_label = Text("(0,0)", font_size=16, color=ORIGIN_COLOR)
        origin_label.next_to(origin_dot, DL, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "Transformations warp space while keeping the origin fixed."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(LINE_HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.play(Create(plane), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(origin_dot), Write(origin_label))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Perform the shear transformation
        shear_matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix),
            run_time=2,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(LINE_HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Flash the grid lines to demonstrate they are parallel and evenly spaced
        # We create temporary lines over the current plane position
        flash_lines = plane.copy().set_color(FLASH_COLOR).set_stroke(width=4)
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(flash_lines, color=FLASH_COLOR, scale_factor=1.02),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.remove(flash_lines)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Imagine stretching a rubber sheet without tearing."
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(LINE_HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        # Add a stretch transformation to simulate the 'rubber sheet' feel
        stretch_matrix = [[1.5, 0], [0, 0.8]] # Stretch X, squish Y slightly
        
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(stretch_matrix),
            # Maintain origin fixed
            origin_dot.animate.move_to(plane.c2p(0, 0)),
            origin_label.animate.next_to(plane.c2p(0, 0), DL, buff=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Clean up highlights for final state
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        for line in lecture_lines:

            lecture_group.add(item)
        
        self.lecture = lecture_group.arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7).shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Right-side Coordinate Grid for Object Placement
        # Mapping grid keys (A1-F6) to spatial coordinates
        self.grid_map = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]
        
        # Define the center and spacing for the right-hand visual area
        center_x = 3.5
        center_y = 0
        spacing = 0.9

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Rows top-to-bottom, Cols left-to-right
                x = center_x + (j - 2.5) * spacing
                y = center_y - (i - 2.5) * spacing
                self.grid_map[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        """Helper to place mobjects on the right-side grid."""
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid_map[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        # Configuration
        title_str = "Linear Transformations & Matrices"
        content = [
            "Matrices as functions",
            "Linear transformation of space",
            "Tracking the basis vectors",
            "The grid remains parallel",
            "Origin remains fixed"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_str, content)

        # Visual Demonstration: Transformation
        # Create a small local coordinate system on the right
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )

        # Basis vectors
        i_hat = Vector([1, 0], color=GREEN).shift(plane.get_origin())
        j_hat = Vector([0, 1], color=RED).shift(plane.get_origin())
        vectors = VGroup(i_hat, j_hat)

        # Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(self.title))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(self.lecture, shift=RIGHT, lag_ratio=0.1),
            run_time=2
        )
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_hat), GrowArrow(j_hat))
        
        # Matrix transformation effect (Shear)
        matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            i_hat.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),

        )
        
        # Highlight a specific grid point
        highlight_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(highlight_dot, "B2", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(Flash(highlight_dot, color=YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(highlight_dot))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title = "Visualizing Matrix-Vector Multiplication"
        lines = [
            "Multiplication scales the new basis vectors.",
            "It is a recipe using transformed basis vectors.",
            "Add these scaled vectors to find the result."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Define Colors
        i_color = "#58C4DD"
        j_color = "#FC6255"

        # Coordinate Plane setup
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'E6')
        
        # Define transformed basis vectors
        # Basis i': [1.0, 0.3], Basis j': [-0.4, 0.8]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        i_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(1, 0.3), buff=0, color=i_color)
        j_vec = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(-0.4, 0.8), buff=0, color=j_color)
        
        # Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        i_label = Text("i'", color=i_color, font_size=20).next_to(i_vec.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        j_label = Text("j'", color=j_color, font_size=20).next_to(j_vec.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_vec), GrowArrow(j_vec), Write(i_label), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # Scale the vectors
        i_vec_scaled = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(3, 0.9), buff=0, color=i_color)
        j_vec_scaled = Arrow(plane.c2p(0, 0), plane.c2p(-0.8, 1.6), buff=0, color=j_color)
        
        i_label_scaled = Text("3i'", color=i_color, font_size=20).next_to(i_vec_scaled.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        j_label_scaled = Text("2j'", color=j_color, font_size=20).next_to(j_vec_scaled.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(i_vec, i_vec_scaled),
            ReplacementTransform(j_vec, j_vec_scaled),
            ReplacementTransform(i_label, i_label_scaled),
            ReplacementTransform(j_label, j_label_scaled)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # Chaining components
        seg_i1 = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1, 0.3), buff=0, color=i_color, stroke_width=3)
        seg_i2 = Arrow(plane.c2p(1, 0.3), plane.c2p(2, 0.6), buff=0, color=i_color, stroke_width=3)
        seg_i3 = Arrow(plane.c2p(2, 0.6), plane.c2p(3, 0.9), buff=0, color=i_color, stroke_width=3)
        
        seg_j1 = Arrow(plane.c2p(3, 0.9), plane.c2p(2.6, 1.7), buff=0, color=j_color, stroke_width=3)
        seg_j2 = Arrow(plane.c2p(2.6, 1.7), plane.c2p(2.2, 2.5), buff=0, color=j_color, stroke_width=3)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(i_label_scaled), FadeOut(j_label_scaled))
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(i_vec_scaled, VGroup(seg_i1, seg_i2, seg_i3)))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(j_vec_scaled, VGroup(seg_j1, seg_j2)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)

        pixel = Dot(plane.c2p(0,0), color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        self.play(FadeIn(pixel))
        
        path_points = [
            plane.c2p(1, 0.3), plane.c2p(2, 0.6), plane.c2p(3, 0.9),
            plane.c2p(2.6, 1.7), plane.c2p(2.2, 2.5)
        ]
        
        for point in path_points:
            self.play(pixel.animate.move_to(point), run_time=0.4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Construct formula using VGroup and Text to bypass LaTeX requirement
        formula = VGroup(
            Text("3", font_size=32),
            Text("i'", font_size=32),
            Text("+", font_size=32),
            Text("2", font_size=32),
            Text("j'", font_size=32),
            Text("=", font_size=32),
            Text("[2.2, 2.5]", font_size=32)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        formula[0].set_color(i_color)
        formula[1].set_color(i_color)
        formula[3].set_color(j_color)
        formula[4].set_color(j_color)
        
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        lecture_lines = [
            "Matrices transform space by moving basis vectors.",
            "Columns are landing spots; determinants are scaling factors.",
            "Visualizing these rules makes linear algebra intuitive."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Intuition Check", lecture_lines)

        # Helper for "Pixel the Cat"
        def get_pixel():
            head = Circle(radius=0.15, color=BLUE_B, fill_opacity=1)
            ear_l = Triangle(color=BLUE_B, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.04).rotate(PI).shift(UP*0.12 + LEFT*0.08)
            ear_r = Triangle(color=BLUE_B, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.04).rotate(PI).shift(UP*0.12 + RIGHT*0.08)
            eye_l = Dot(radius=0.02, color=BLACK).shift(LEFT*0.05 + UP*0.02)
            eye_r = Dot(radius=0.02, color=BLACK).shift(RIGHT*0.05 + UP*0.02)
            return VGroup(head, ear_l, ear_r, eye_l, eye_r)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Icons for vector, matrix, determinant
        vec_icon = Arrow(start=LEFT*0.3, end=RIGHT*0.3, color=YELLOW)
        
        # Replace MathTex with Text-based objects to avoid LaTeX FileNotFoundError
        mat_elements = VGroup(
            Text("a", font_size=22), Text("b", font_size=22),
            Text("c", font_size=22), Text("d", font_size=22)
        ).arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=2, buff=0.3)
        mat_bracket_l = Text("[", font_size=42).scale(np.array([0.7, 1.3, 1])).next_to(mat_elements, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        mat_bracket_r = Text("]", font_size=42).scale(np.array([0.7, 1.3, 1])).next_to(mat_elements, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        mat_icon = VGroup(mat_bracket_l, mat_elements, mat_bracket_r).set_color(YELLOW)
        
        det_icon = Text("det(A)", font_size=22, color=YELLOW)
        
        icons = VGroup(vec_icon, mat_icon, det_icon).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(icons, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(icons))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(TEAL)
        self.play(FadeOut(icons))

        # Gallery of three quick grid transformations
        # 1. Rotation
        plane1 = NumberPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], x_length=2, y_length=2, 
                            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4})
        pixel1 = get_pixel()
        gal1 = VGroup(plane1, pixel1)
        self.place_in_area(gal1, "C1", "D2", scale_factor=0.7)
        label1 = Text("Rotation", font_size=16).next_to(gal1, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # 2. Shear
        plane2 = NumberPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], x_length=2, y_length=2, 
                            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4})
        pixel2 = get_pixel()
        gal2 = VGroup(plane2, pixel2)
        self.place_in_area(gal2, "C3", "D4", scale_factor=0.7)
        label2 = Text("Shear", font_size=16).next_to(gal2, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # 3. Flip
        plane3 = NumberPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], x_length=2, y_length=2, 
                            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4})
        pixel3 = get_pixel()
        gal3 = VGroup(plane3, pixel3)
        self.place_in_area(gal3, "C5", "D6", scale_factor=0.7)
        label3 = Text("Flip", font_size=16).next_to(gal3, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        gallery = VGroup(gal1, label1, gal2, label2, gal3, label3)
        self.play(FadeIn(gallery))

        # Perform the transformations
        rot_mat = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]
        shear_mat = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        flip_mat = [[-1, 0], [0, 1]]

        self.play(
            gal1.animate.apply_matrix(rot_mat),
            gal2.animate.apply_matrix(shear_mat),
            gal3.animate.apply_matrix(flip_mat),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        
        final_text = Text("The Visual Language of Matrices", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(final_text, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(gallery),
            FadeIn(final_text)
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Visual Language of Matrices: Geometric Intuition in Linear Algebra
outline.target_audience: First-year university students or STEM-focused high school students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Vector as a Path
sections.content: Introduce vectors not as a list of numbers, but as a movement in space starting from the origin (0,0). Establish the 'Unit Basis Vectors' (i-hat and j-hat) as the fundamental building blocks of the 2D plane.
sections.example: Pixel the Cat starts at (0,0). Moving 3 units along the x-axis and 2 units along the y-axis is represented as the vector [3, 2]. We see this as a bright arrow pointing to Pixel's new position.

sections.title: The Concept of Linear Transformation
sections.content: Define a transformation as a function that takes in one vector and spits out another. 'Linear' means the origin remains fixed and all grid lines remain parallel and evenly spaced. Use animation to show the grid warping.
sections.example: Imagine Pixel's entire world is printed on a rubber sheet. A linear transformation is like stretching or rotating that sheet without tearing it or curving the grid lines.

sections.title: The Matrix as a 'Landing Map'
sections.content: Explain that to track where *any* vector goes, we only need to track where the basis vectors (i-hat and j-hat) land. A 2x2 matrix is simply a record of these two landing spots. The first column is where i-hat landed; the second column is where j-hat landed.
sections.example: If i-hat [1, 0] lands at [1, 1] and j-hat [0, 1] lands at [-2, 0], the matrix describing this transformation is [[1, -2], [1, 0]]. We see the grid 'skew' and 'tilt' based on these new landing points.

sections.title: Visualizing Matrix-Vector Multiplication
sections.content: Show that multiplying a matrix by a vector is just a 'weighted sum' of the transformed basis vectors. It is a recipe for finding where Pixel ends up in the warped world.
sections.example: To find where Pixel [3, 2] goes, we take 3 units of the 'new' i-hat and 2 units of the 'new' j-hat. We animate the arrows chaining together to find Pixel's final transformed position.

sections.title: The Determinant: The Scaling Factor
sections.content: Introduce the determinant as the factor by which areas change during the transformation. If the determinant is 2, the area doubles. If it's 0, the world squishes into a line or a point.
sections.example: Pixel is sitting on a 1x1 square rug. After the transformation, if the rug now covers an area of 3 units, the determinant of our matrix is 3. If the rug becomes a flat line, Pixel has no room to move, and the determinant is 0.

sections.title: Summary & Intuition Check
sections.content: Recap the flow: Vectors are points -> Matrices are transformations -> Columns are basis vector destinations -> Determinants are area scales.
sections.example: Animate a quick 'gallery' of transformations: a rotation, a shear, and a flip, showing Pixel the Cat reacting to each change in his coordinate world.
